Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: No documented integration of CRVS with a government data exchange platform in Niger.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The cited numericite.eu source covers only the 2020-22 e-gov/portal strategy and does not address CRVS data-exchange integration. A 2023 AfDB/COMESA CRVS digitalisation assessment (fetched) confirmed Niger then had no digitised national identity system and no CRVS-ID interoperability. However, the World Bank-financed WURI-Niger project (Composante 3) is financing an interoperability framework linking the National Population Register/ID system with the état civil (CRVS) system; a February 2026 project mission (fetched) confirms active work aligning the Registre National de la Population with état civil and designing the target architecture, via a newly formed inter-institutional Task Force. This is active but not operational, so recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development).
revised_comments: The Registre National de la Population is being aligned with Niger's état civil (CRVS) system under the World Bank-financed WURI-Niger project. A digital état civil management platform already operates in around 100 communes, recording births and assigning unique identification numbers, but full interoperability between CRVS and the national identification system remains under design: a February 2026 project mission set out the target technical architecture and formed an inter-institutional Task Force, coordinated by ANSI, to advance this work. CRVS data is therefore not yet integrated into an operational cross-government data exchange.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: No evidence of a national digital ID integrated with a data exchange platform in Niger. Digital identity systems are not yet documented as part of an interoperability framework.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original source does not address digital ID-to-exchange integration. Niger has no fully deployed national digital ID yet, but the World Bank-financed WURI-Niger project is developing a foundational ID (Numéro Unique d'Identification) on the MOSIP platform; a pilot enrolling ~500 people was completed via 'Lab MOSIP', and a February 2026 mission (fetched) progressed the target technical architecture and governance for a future National Registration and Identification Agency. The interoperability layer intended to connect the ID with other service providers (Composante 3) is financed but not operational. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development).
revised_comments: Niger does not yet have a fully deployed national digital identity system integrated into a cross-government data exchange. The World Bank-financed WURI-Niger project is developing a foundational digital ID based on the MOSIP open-source platform; a pilot enrolling around 500 people has been completed through the 'Lab MOSIP', and a February 2026 project mission advanced the target technical architecture and governance arrangements for a future National Registration and Identification Agency (ANEI). The interoperability layer intended to connect the digital ID with other public and private service providers is financed but not yet operational.

redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. No operational, whole-of-government data exchange platform currently exists in Niger for sub-national governments to participate in; digital government initiatives (ANSI's e-services portal, WURI-Niger's planned ID/interoperability framework) remain centrally managed and are still under development. No authoritative source describes sub-national government participation in any data exchange, so the 'n.a.' component of code 0 continues to apply rather than a definitive '1=National level only', which would imply an existing exchange restricted to national actors.
revised_comments: No government data exchange platform currently operates in Niger with which sub-national administrations could participate. Digital government initiatives, including the citizen services portal managed by the Agence Nationale pour la Société de l'Information (ANSI) and the World Bank-financed WURI-Niger identification and interoperability project, remain centrally managed and are still under development.

The WURI-Niger identity and interoperability project, whose governance structures (including a newly formed inter-institutional Task Force) were still being defined as of February 2026, has not yet published data-sharing agreements or transparency reporting on any exchange mechanism.
